intro: Udon Thani's 2026 list is six Bib Gourmand kitchens and no stars, but this is exactly the food locals grew up on. Start with Kao.Piak.Sen, a Vietnamese-style rice-noodle soup for around 60 baht, then work through Peng Duck Noodles and the punchy Isan cooking at Krua Khun Nid. It is a whole city of good eating on a friendly budget.

faq.q: How many Michelin restaurants does Udon Thani have in 2026?
faq.a: Six, all Bib Gourmand and no stars yet: Kao.Piak.Sen, Khao Soi Thai Yai, Krua Khun Nid, Majchapasuk, Pad Thai Bua Dang and Peng Duck Noodles.

faq.q: Which one is the cheapest and easiest to try?
faq.a: Kao.Piak.Sen, a Vietnamese-style rice-noodle soup at around 60 baht a bowl, is the best-value pick. Peng Duck Noodles and Khao Soi Thai Yai also land around 50 to 90 baht.

faq.q: Where should I go for real Isan food?
faq.a: Krua Khun Nid is the Isan kitchen on this list, cooking bold local flavors at roughly 250 to 500 baht per meal, and it is built for ordering a spread to share.

faq.q: We're a group and want dishes to share. Where should I book?
faq.a: Majchapasuk serves Thai sharing plates in the low hundreds of baht per dish, made for a table of friends, while Krua Khun Nid works well for a shared Isan spread. Call ahead on weekends.

faq.q: What's something unusual I can't easily find elsewhere?
faq.a: The rice-noodle soup at Kao.Piak.Sen carries a Vietnamese accent that Udon does especially well, and Khao Soi Thai Yai is a Northern-style khao soi you rarely see in Isan. Both taste distinctly of this city.
